agenda: the choice: fuel expedition, antibiotic expedition, or Kilo water rescue

decisions.item: the choice: fuel expedition, antibiotic expedition, or Kilo water rescue
decisions.outcome: the_general presented the three-way choice prepared by the_quartermaster (supply_audit_b3_010). Fuel at 15 days. Antibiotics at zero. Kilo settlement at 2 days of water, 12 souls, 2 children. the_quartermaster stated the bunker cannot do all three and may be able to do one. the_surgeon spoke for antibiotics: one infection, one funeral. the_electrician spoke for fuel: without power, ventilation and cold storage fail, and the antibiotic question becomes moot. the_priest spoke for Kilo: a well that fails is a death sentence and a death sentence is everyone's business. the_therapist did not speak for an option; she said the decision will cost the decider regardless of which is chosen, and the council should know that. the_courier, invited for the first time, said: if we go to Kilo, I will go. If we do not go, I will listen for them until the radio stops. the_hunter said the Freeholder's free water guide removes half the return risk. the vote was not unanimous. The council chose Kilo.

the_general reported the_courier's Day 163 mission (courier_mission_b2_010). the_Freeholder confirmed Kilo at 18km east of Settlement 2, beyond Freeholder patrol range. the_Freeholder offered a free water guide for the return route. the council accepted the guide offer. the_cop raised the security risk of an external guide knowing the bunker-to-Kilo route. the_general said the guide knows Settlement 2 to Kilo, not the bunker; the bunker team meets the guide at Settlement 2. the_cop accepted.

the_general ordered a Kilo water assistance mission departing Day 167, returning Day 170 (est.). Team: the_courier, the_hunter, the_plumber (well assessment), the_quartermaster (water ration allocation). Route: bunker to Settlement 2 (10km, Day 1), Settlement 2 to Kilo with guide (18km, Day 2), Kilo water delivery and well assessment (Day 3), return via Settlement 2 (Day 4). Load: 4 water containers (80L treated cistern water), water filtration kit, well tools, 5kg dried mushrooms (goodwill), 2kg salt (goodwill). the_hunter carries the rifle. the_courier carries the hand-crank radio. Fuel cost: 0 litres (foot mission, no vehicle). the_quartermaster confirmed the bunker can spare 80L without dropping below 50 days cistern supply.

items.notes: The first council decision that was not unanimous. the_electrician voted against — not against Kilo, against the fuel arithmetic. He said: 'I am not voting against children. I am voting for the generator. If the generator stops, the children in this bunker are also at risk.' His vote was recorded and respected. the_surgeon and the_architect abstained because they could not rank the three options and chose not to pretend. the_general said after the vote: 'A non-unanimous council is a council that is doing its work. A unanimous council is a council that has stopped thinking.' the_therapist, who did not speak for an option, watched the_general during the vote. She has a session with him on Day 172. This is the first decision the bunker has made that costs something to someone inside it in order to help someone outside it. the_priest said a prayer after the vote. No one objected. No one joined him. He said it anyway.

agenda: fuel constraint — 17 days, the operational ceiling
antibiotic constraint — zero doses, the silent second constraint
expedition options and the order of risk

decisions.item: fuel constraint — 17 days, the operational ceiling
decisions.outcome: the_quartermaster reported fuel at 175 litres, 17 days at current consumption (10L/day). the_electrician confirmed the voltage regulator is on its final channel; the next channel failure forces permanent load-shedding. the_electrician stated: if we do nothing, the generator stops in 17 days. When the generator stops, ventilation stops, cold storage stops, the radio stops, the grow lights stop. the_botanist confirmed the grow lights stopping ends the barley cycle and the wheat cycle — the greenhouse reverts to ambient winter light, which is insufficient. the_courier mission to Kilo cost zero fuel because it was on foot. the_quartermaster stated: foot missions buy time but do not buy fuel. Fuel is the one resource we cannot produce and cannot trade for. the_council agreed fuel is the binding constraint and must be addressed before the antibiotic constraint, because without power the antibiotic question is academic.

decisions.item: antibiotic constraint — zero doses, the silent second constraint
decisions.outcome: the_surgeon reported antibiotics remain at zero. Painkillers at 22 doses. Bandages at 140. Antiseptic at 1.5 litres. the_chemist reported the iodide stock is improved (supply_audit_b3_003) but iodide is not antibiotics and does not address bacterial infection. the_surgeon stated: the bunker has been lucky. Seven dysentery cases, no deaths. One wound infection on Day 88, treated with antiseptic and hope, resolved. The luck is not a strategy. the_next infection that does not resolve on its own is a death the bunker has chosen to accept by inaction. the_quartermaster noted the hospital pharmacy (exp_report_abandoned_hospital_01) was high-radiation and partially looted; the agri supply depot second store is unconfirmed. the_council agreed antibiotics are the second priority, immediately after fuel, and the expedition must target a confirmed pharmaceutical source.

decisions.item: expedition options and the order of risk
decisions.outcome: the_general presented two fuel expedition options and one antibiotic expedition option. (1) Train yard diesel residue recovery — the locomotive tank was siphoned by another party, but the Veteran reported a frozen diesel pool under the locomotive; the Chemist believes 20-40 litres of contaminated diesel may be recoverable and filterable. Risk: other party may return. Fuel cost: 2 days. (2) Signal lamp oil — 12 tins recovered (exp_report_train_yard_01), pending Chemist suitability test; if suitable, extends lamp oil reserve but is not generator fuel. (3) Antibiotic expedition — the Chemist identified a pre-war pharmaceutical distribution warehouse on the Cartographer's map, 14km southwest, radiation unconfirmed. Risk: unknown dose, possible looting. Fuel cost: 3 days. the_council debated the order. the_electrician argued for fuel first — without power the antibiotic expedition cannot be planned (radio, lights, cold storage). the_surgeon argued for antibiotics first — the fuel buys days, the antibiotics buy lives, and a life lost to infection while the fuel burns down is the worst outcome. the_general broke the deadlock: fuel first, antibiotics second, because the fuel expedition is lower-risk and higher-certainty, and a dead generator makes the antibiotic expedition a suicide run. the_council accepted.
decisions.vote: 7_for_2_abstain (the_surgeon and the_priest abstained — the_priest said he could not rank fuel above medicine and could not rank medicine above fuel and would not pretend)

action_items: the_chemist: complete signal lamp oil suitability test by Day 174 — if suitable, allocate to lamp reserve; if not, report
the_chemist: assess train yard diesel residue filterability — can contaminated diesel be cleaned to generator-grade? Report by Day 175

the_chemist: cross-reference the Cartographer's map for the pharmaceutical distribution warehouse — confirm location, estimate radiation, plan approach. Report by Day 178
the_electrician: prepare the load-shed schedule for the fuel crisis — what runs, what does not, in 5-day decrements from Day 180
the_quartermaster: maintain the fuel ledger daily — no expedition departs without the_quartermaster's fuel accounting
items.notes: The first council meeting since the Kilo decision (council_minutes_016) that returned to unanimous on the constraints and split only on the order. The split is honest. the_surgeon abstained because he will not rank fuel above lives. the_priest abstained because he will not rank anything above anything. the_general said after the vote: 'We are not choosing between fuel and antibiotics. We are choosing the order in which we fail at both, and hoping we do not fail at either.' the_therapist watched the_general. She had a session with him at 14:00 before this meeting (therapy_session_b3_008). She noted he went to the airlock yesterday without deciding to. She did not tell the council. the_hunter asked, after the meeting, whether the wolf pack would be a problem on the train yard return. the_general said carry two rifles. the_hunter said he has one. the_general said he knows. The meeting did not resolve the rifle question. It resolved the order. The order is fuel, then antibiotics, then whatever comes after, if anything does.

decisions.item: diesel confirmation — 30 litres approved, fuel ceiling Day 195
decisions.outcome: the_chemist confirmed the recovered diesel is generator-grade (chem_lab_003). 30 litres approved for generator use. Fuel reserve now 205 litres, 20 days at current consumption (10L/day). Fuel ceiling extended from Day 192 to Day 195. the_electrician reported the generator accepted the blend without alarm. the_quartermaster logged the fuel. the_general stated: this is three days. It is not a solution. It is the time we have to solve the antibiotic question.

decisions.item: antibiotic expedition — pharmaceutical distribution warehouse, 14km southwest
decisions.outcome: the_chemist presented the warehouse reconnaissance: the Cartographer's map marks a pre-war pharmaceutical distribution warehouse at 14km southwest, grid reference confirmed. Radiation unconfirmed — no prior visit. the_chemist estimates the warehouse, if intact, may contain antibiotic stock (amoxicillin, doxycycline, ciprofloxacin) in sealed manufacturer packaging. the_surgeon provided the target list: broad-spectrum antibiotics first, then analgesics, then suture material, then IV fluids if present. the_veteran assessed the route: 14km southwest via the ridge, 2-day outbound, 1 day on site, 2-day return — 5-day mission. the_hunter assessed the wolf risk: the southwestern ridge is outside the current pack range but not guaranteed. the_general ordered the expedition. Team: the_veteran (leader), the_courier, the_mechanic, the_hunter. the_surgeon did not volunteer — single-provider logic accepted (therapy_session_b3_010). the_chemist stays with the lab. Departure Day 183.

decisions.item: grow light bulb crisis — greenhouse at risk
decisions.outcome: the_mechanic (invited) reported grow light bed A is now on a single bulb at extended hours (maint_log_b3_010). No spare bulbs. If the last bulb fails, the greenhouse reverts to ambient winter light — insufficient for barley and wheat cycles. the_botanist (reported by the_mechanic) states the wheat cycle is the priority and the wheat is on bed B. the_electrician proposed an LED retrofit from the fire lookout hand-crank radio indicator circuit — speculative, low output, may extend one bed by 10-20 percent. the_council approved the LED retrofit as a research priority and authorised a grow-light-bulb search on the next expedition. the_quartermaster noted no known source. the_general stated: the greenhouse is the long-term food solution. If the grow lights fail, the long term becomes the short term.

decisions.item: the other salvage party — train yard assessment
decisions.outcome: the_veteran reported the train yard was empty during the diesel recovery (courier_mission_b2_015, b2_016). No new boot prints. The other party has not returned in 12 days. the_veteran assessment: the party has either moved on, exhausted the site, or is observing from a distance. the_cop raised the possibility the party is monitoring the bunker's expedition pattern. the_general stated: we do not have evidence of surveillance. We have evidence of absence. Absence is not safety. the_council agreed to vary expedition departure times and routes where possible. the_cop to brief the perimeter team.

He provided the medical target list and did not speak about the abstention. the_therapist, who had a session with the_surgeon on Day 184 (therapy_session_b3_010, scheduled after this meeting), watched him. She did not speak. the_general noted the grow light crisis is the third constraint — fuel, antibiotics, and now light. He said: 'We are juggling three things and we have two hands.' the_quartermaster said, 'Then we catch one and let the other two fall and pick them up after.' the_general said, 'Which one do we catch first.' the_quartermaster said, 'The one that is closest to the ground.' No one specified which one that was. The meeting ended with the order: warehouse expedition Day 183, LED research Day 188, and the understanding that the fuel ceiling is Day 195 and everything must be resolved or extended by then.

agri supply depot return — grow light bulb search
fuel countdown — Day 195 ceiling, 6 days remaining

decisions.outcome: the_chemist confirmed all 304 antibiotic doses are viable (chem_lab_004). All within labelled shelf life (14-22 months future). Packaging intact. The reserve must be conserved. The reserve is not a license to be reckless. the_council accepted the report.

decisions.item: grow light crisis — the third constraint, now the primary
decisions.outcome: the_electrician reported the LED retrofit (maint_log_b3_012) is complete but provides only 5 percent of a single grow light bulb's output. the_botanist (invited) reported the last functional bulb on bed B (barley) began flickering on Day 188 (journal_raw_b3_23). the_botanist estimates the bulb has 3-7 days of life. When it fails, the greenhouse reverts to LED-only at 5 percent output. the_botanist stated: at 5 percent output, the wheat seedlings (the Tomas wheat, journal_raw_b3_12) will survive but not thrive. The barley cycle will fail. The turnip cycle will slow. Greenhouse production drops from 14 percent to an estimated 3-4 percent of caloric need. the_quartermaster stated: 3-4 percent is not a food supply. It is a garnish. the_general stated: the grow light is now the primary constraint. Fuel is Day 195 (6 days). Antibiotics are addressed. The grow light is the thing that determines whether the bunker eats in 90 days.

decisions.item: agri supply depot return — grow light bulb search
decisions.outcome: the_mechanic proposed a return to the agri supply depot (exp_report_agri_supply_depot_01) to search the unsearched second store behind the heaved wall (the first visit recovered potassium chloride, lime, fleece, and seeders but did not breach the second store). The second store may contain grow light bulbs — the depot was an agricultural supply depot and grow lights are a plausible stock item. the_chemist concurs: the depot's inventory is unknown and the second store is the highest-probability source of grow light bulbs within walking distance. the_veteran assessed the route: 12km northwest, 2-day mission, low risk (the first visit was uneventful). the_general ordered the expedition. Team: the_mechanic (leader, breaching), the_courier (carry, rear security), the_hunter (overwatch), the_electrician (grow light bulb identification and electrical assessment). Departure Day 191.

decisions.item: fuel countdown — Day 195 ceiling, 6 days remaining
decisions.outcome: the_quartermaster reported fuel at 205 litres, 20 days supply, but the agri depot return is a foot mission (0 fuel cost). the_electrician reported the generator is running on the recovered diesel blend without alarm. the_general stated: the fuel ceiling is Day 195. The agri depot mission returns Day 193. The bunker has 2 days of margin between the mission return and the fuel ceiling. If the grow light bulbs are recovered, the greenhouse continues. If they are not, the greenhouse drops to 3-4 percent and the bunker's food trajectory reverses. the_council acknowledged the fuel ceiling is unchanged and the grow light expedition is the priority within it.

The grow light is the primary. the_botanist spoke for the first time in council since the greenhouse first harvest (council_minutes_015). She said the word 'garnish' was the_quartermaster's, not hers. She said her word is 'proof.' The wheat is the proof. The barley is the practice. If the bulb fails, the proof survives at 5 percent. The practice does not. She said she can accept that. She said she does not accept it gracefully. the_therapist watched the_botanist. She has scheduled a session with the_botanist on Day 192 (therapy_session_b3_011). the_general said after the vote: 'We have three constraints. One is addressed. One is counting down. agenda: grow light resolved — the third constraint is addressed
fuel countdown — Day 208 ceiling, 13 days remaining, now the primary and only unresolved constraint
fuel expedition options — the geo-thermal plant and beyond

decisions.item: grow light resolved — the third constraint is addressed
decisions.outcome: the_botanist confirmed the greenhouse is running on a new T8 tube (courier_mission_b2_022). 12 tubes and 5 ballasts in reserve (exp_report_agri_supply_depot_02). Estimated 18-24 months of grow light capacity. The barley cycle continues. The wheat cycle continues. The greenhouse is at 15 percent of caloric need and climbing. the_quartermaster stated: the cliff has been moved. It is no longer the cliff. It is a shelf. The shelf holds for 18-24 months. the_council acknowledged the resolution.

decisions.item: fuel countdown — Day 208 ceiling, 13 days remaining, now the primary and only unresolved constraint
decisions.outcome: the_quartermaster reported fuel at 135 litres, 13 days at current consumption (10L/day). Ceiling Day 208. The antibiotics are a reserve (holding). The grow lights are a shelf (holding). The fuel is a countdown (running). The fuel is now the only constraint that is not addressed. the_electrician reported the generator is running on the recovered diesel blend without alarm but the voltage regulator is on its final channel (maint_log_b3_002). the_general stated: the fuel is the last countdown. If it reaches zero, the generator stops, the ventilation stops, the cold storage stops, the radio stops, the grow lights stop. The grow light shelf becomes irrelevant if the generator stops. The antibiotic reserve becomes harder to use without power. The fuel is the constraint that holds all other constraints. the_council agreed the fuel is the primary and the fuel expedition is the priority.

the_electrician presented the load-shed schedule (load_shed_schedule_001, to be filed separately). The schedule defines, in 2-day decrements from Day 208, what runs and what does not when the generator fuel reaches zero. Priority 1 (last to shed): medical bay cold storage, ventilation. Priority 2: comms (radio). Priority 3: greenhouse grow lights. Priority 4: corridor heat. Priority 5: mess hall, laundry. The schedule also defines the manual fallback for each system: ventilation (manual air-handling, 4-person rotation), water (gravity feed from the cistern, no pump), cold storage (insulated, passive — 2-day window), grow lights (LED array at 5 percent, battery). the_council accepted the schedule as the governing document for the final days. the_electrician stated: the schedule is not a plan to survive without fuel. It is a plan to extend the fuel we have by choosing what we do without.

decisions.item: fuel expedition options — the geo-thermal plant and beyond
decisions.outcome: the_mechanic proposed a return to the geo-thermal plant (exp_report_geo_thermal_plant_01, first visit Day 50). The first visit recovered pipe, gaskets, and a technical manual but did not assess the plant's fuel or lubricant stock — the visit focused on the steam system. the_mechanic believes the plant's maintenance shed may contain diesel or lubricant stock for the turbine system. the_chemist concurs: a geo-thermal plant requires backup diesel for the startup cycle and maintenance fuel; the shed is a plausible source. the_veteran assessed the route: 8km south-southwest, 2-day mission, moderate radiation (45 uSv/h at the turbine hall, 3-hour max exposure). the_general ordered the expedition. Team: the_mechanic (leader), the_courier, the_hunter, the_chemist (fuel assessment on site — the_chemist overcomes the fear of the sky for the fuel, therapy_session_b3_010 context). Departure Day 197. the_general also ordered the_chemist and the_quartermaster to identify a second fuel source beyond the geo-thermal plant — the train yard is exhausted, the geo-thermal plant is a single visit. The bunker needs a fuel source that is not a single visit.

items.notes: The council meeting where the constraints reduced to one. The antibiotics are a reserve. The grow lights are a shelf. The fuel is a countdown. The countdown is the one. the_quartermaster said: 'We have a reserve, a countdown, and a cliff, and the cliff has been moved. The cliff is a shelf. The shelf holds. The reserve holds. The countdown runs. The countdown is the only one that moves.' the_general said: 'Then the countdown is the one we move.' the_therapist watched the_general. She has a session with him after this meeting (therapy_session_b3_012). She noted he said 'we move' not 'I move.' That is new. the_priest said a short prayer at the end. No one joined him. No one objected. He said it anyway. The meeting ended with the order: geo-thermal plant fuel expedition Day 197, load-shed schedule filed, second fuel source identified by Day 200, and the understanding that Day 208 is the ceiling and the ceiling is 13 days and 13 days is the time the bunker has to find fuel or learn to live without it.

agenda: the fuel decision — what happens at Day 208
the Bouncer observation — the thing that watches the wolves

decisions.outcome: the_mechanic reported the geo-thermal plant expedition (courier_mission_b2_023, b2_024) recovered 45 litres of diesel from the maintenance shed backup tank and 8 litres of lubricant. the_chemist confirmed the diesel is generator-grade (chem_lab_005). Fuel reserve now 95 litres (post-consumption), 9 days at current consumption. Ceiling extended from Day 208 to Day 212. the_quartermaster logged the fuel. the_general stated: 45 litres is 4 days. It is another breath. The ceiling moves. The countdown does not stop.

the_quartermaster reported the second fuel source search. The Cartographer's map and the fire finder map (exp_report_fire_lookout_01) were cross-referenced. Two candidates identified: (1) a municipal fuel depot 18km southeast, marked on the fire finder map as a 'fuel storage' site — radiation unknown, distance is at the edge of the walkable range. (2) a pre-war hospital backup generator fuel tank (the hospital was visited exp_report_abandoned_hospital_01, but the basement generator room was not accessed due to high radiation — 120 uSv/h). the_chemist assessed: the hospital tank is too hot (120 uSv/h, lethal exposure in under 4 hours). The municipal fuel depot is the only viable candidate. the_veteran assessed: 18km, 3-day mission, moderate-high risk (distance, unknown radiation, unknown structural condition). the_general stated: the municipal fuel depot is the next expedition. It is the last identified fuel source within walkable range. If it is empty or too hot, the bunker has no further fuel source and the load-shed schedule becomes the survival plan.

decisions.item: the fuel decision — what happens at Day 208
decisions.outcome: the_electrician presented the load-shed schedule implementation status (maint_log_b3_017). The schedule is posted. The manual ventilation rotation is trained (the_plumber, 4-person roster). The manual water fallback (gravity feed) is tested. The cold storage passive window (2 days) is documented. the_general asked the question the council has been avoiding: what happens at Day 212 (the new ceiling) if the municipal fuel depot yields nothing. the_electrician stated: at Day 212, the generator stops. The load-shed schedule has already shed corridors, laundry, mess hall. At Day 212, the grow lights go off. The medical cold storage goes passive (2-day window). The radio goes to hand-crank only. The ventilation goes manual. the_surgeon stated: the medical cold storage passive window is 2 days. After 2 days, the antibiotic reserve must be stored in the coldest part of the bunker (the lower corridor, estimated 8C) and the viability may degrade. the_botanist stated: the grow lights going off means the greenhouse drops to LED-only at 5 percent. The wheat survives. The barley does not. The food trajectory reverses. the_general stated: the bunker has been living on breaths. The breaths are running out. The municipal fuel depot is the last breath. If it is not there, the bunker learns to live without the generator. the_council agreed: the municipal fuel depot expedition is the priority. The load-shed schedule is the fallback. The fallback is not a plan. It is a way of dying slowly. The expedition is the plan.

decisions.item: the Bouncer observation — the thing that watches the wolves
decisions.outcome: the_cop reported the investigation of the Bouncer's statement (patrol_debrief_024, 'I am afraid of the thing that watches the wolves'). the_cop and the_veteran conducted a dawn observation of the southwestern ridge on Day 201 (patrol_debrief_026). the_veteran observed, at 600m, a figure on the ridge watching the wolf pack. The figure was stationary, did not move, did not approach. the_veteran could not confirm if the figure was human or a trick of the light. the_hunter, on a separate observation Day 202, confirmed: a stationary figure, human-shaped, at 700m, watching the wolves. The figure withdrew when the wolves moved. the_cop stated: the Bouncer was right. There is something watching the wolves. The something is human or human-shaped. It does not approach. It watches. the_general stated: a human who watches wolves and does not approach is a human who is assessing. Assessing is preparation. Preparation is either hunting or scouting. the_council agreed: the southwestern ridge is now a restricted approach. No solo patrols. No expedition routes via the southwest. the_cop and the_veteran to continue dawn observation. the_therapist to assess the Bouncer — the statement was not paranoia. It was perception.

Day 192 to 195 to 208 to 212. Each extension is a breath. Each breath is shorter. The breaths are not a strategy. The breaths are a habit. A habit is a thing that does not ask permission. I am grateful for the habit. I am afraid of the day the habit runs out.' the_general said: 'The municipal fuel depot is the last breath. If it is not there, we stop breathing and we start living without the generator. Living without the generator is possible. It is harder. It is colder. It is quieter. The bunker has done harder things.' the_priest said: 'The bunker has done harder things.' He said it as a statement, not a prayer. The meeting ended with the order: municipal fuel depot expedition Day 205, the southwestern ridge restricted, the Bouncer vindicated, and the understanding that Day 212 is the ceiling and the ceiling is 9 days and 9 days is the time the bunker has to find the last breath or learn to live without breathing.

the depot as a source — standing monthly recovery trips
the spring — the Cartographer's report, the ash thinning

decisions.item: municipal fuel depot success — 900 litres, the fuel ceiling lifted
decisions.outcome: the_veteran reported the municipal fuel depot expedition (courier_mission_b2_025, b2_026, exp_report_municipal_fuel_depot_01). The depot is intact, 4 uSv/h, 2 underground tanks, 900 litres total (80 recovered, 820 remaining). the_chemist confirmed the recovered diesel is generator-grade (chem_lab_006, pending). the_quartermaster logged the 80 litres. Fuel reserve now 155 litres (75 remaining + 80 recovered), 15 days at current consumption, but the 820 litres in the depot represent 82 days of additional fuel. The fuel ceiling is no longer a countdown. The fuel ceiling is the depot's exhaustion, which is months away at monthly recovery trips. the_general stated: the last breath was not the last. The last breath was the first of many. The fuel is no longer the constraint. The fuel is a source.

decisions.item: the depot as a source — standing monthly recovery trips
decisions.outcome: the_quartermaster proposed a standing monthly fuel recovery trip to the municipal depot. Each trip: 4-person team, 3 days, 80 litres recovered (the carry capacity). At 10L/day consumption, each trip is 8 days of fuel, and the depot holds 10 more trips. The depot is the fuel source for the next 10 months. the_veteran confirmed the route is known, the dose is low, and the depot is intact. the_general approved the standing trip. the_quartermaster to schedule the next depot trip for Day 240. the_council agreed the fuel constraint is resolved for the foreseeable future, contingent on the depot remaining intact and unlooted.

the_cop reported the Cartographer contact (patrol_debrief_027, letter_b2_26). The Cartographer confirmed the depot has fuel, the wolves are not a threat, the ash is thinning, and the spring is coming. The Cartographer will meet a bunker person at the cache on Day 220. the_general stated: the Cartographer is the first external person to offer the bunker a relationship since the Freeholder on Day 100. The Cartographer has maps, knowledge of the wasteland, and knowledge of the spring. The meeting is the priority. the_council discussed who goes. the_general proposed the_courier — the Courier is the bunker's walker, the youngest, the least threatening, and the one who carried the note to the cache. the_therapist concurred — the Courier has the relational capacity for a first contact. the_hunter offered to provide overwatch from a distance. the_general approved: the_courier meets the Cartographer at the cache on Day 220, the_hunter on overwatch at 300m, no one else. The meeting is a diplomatic contact, not a patrol.

decisions.item: the spring — the Cartographer's report, the ash thinning
decisions.outcome: the_meteorologist (invited, reported by the_quartermaster) confirmed the Cartographer's claim: barometric pressure has been rising for 14 days, the wind has shifted to the southwest, and the ash particulate density has dropped 30 percent since Day 180. the_meteorologist estimates the surface dose in the low-dose zones will be plantable by Day 250-260. the_botanist (invited) confirmed the greenhouse wheat is 30 days from harvest and the barley is 45 days. If the spring permits outdoor planting, the bunker's food production moves from the greenhouse to the surface. the_quartermaster stated: the spring is the thing that changes everything. The fuel is a source. The antibiotics are a reserve. The grow lights are a shelf. The spring is the thing that makes the greenhouse a bridge instead of a destination. the_general stated: the bunker has been surviving for 210 days. The spring is when the bunker begins to live.

The spring is coming. the_quartermaster said: 'I have been keeping the ledger for 176 days and the ledger has been a document of things going down. Today the ledger has a thing that goes up. The fuel is a source. The source is the thing that does not go down. The source is the thing that stays.' the_general said: 'The bunker has been surviving. The spring is when the bunker begins to live.' the_priest said: 'The spring is when the chapel fills.' He said it as a statement. The meeting ended with the order: Cartographer meeting Day 220, depot trip Day 240, spring tracking weekly, and the understanding that the bunker's second winter is ending and the thing that comes after survival is the thing the bunker has not yet named.

agenda: the questions — what the bunker asks
the gifts — what the bunker brings
the protocol — how the meeting is conducted

decisions.outcome: the_general confirmed the meeting: the_courier at the Cartographer's cache on Day 220, the_hunter on overwatch at 300m. the_courier departs Day 219, arrives at the cache Day 220 morning. the_hunter departs Day 219, positions at the overwatch before dawn. the_courier carries the hand-crank radio for emergency broadcast only — no transmission during the meeting. the meeting is face-to-face. the_courier is the bunker's voice. the_hunter is the bunker's eye. No one else.

decisions.item: the questions — what the bunker asks
decisions.outcome: the_council compiled the question list for the Cartographer. (1) The maps — can the Cartographer share the maps of the fuel, water, low-dose zones, and the spring? (2) The spring — when will the surface be plantable, and which zones? (3) The wolves — will the pack return, or is the southwest migration permanent? (4) The other settlements — the Cartographer walks the wasteland; what settlements exist, and what are their relations? (5) The Verge — the Lineman reported the Verge has lost power (rad_lineman_04); does the Cartographer know the Verge, and can the bunker help? (6) The Cartographer's needs — what does the Cartographer need that the bunker can offer? the_therapist added: the last question is the one that makes the meeting a relationship instead of an interrogation. the_general accepted.

decisions.item: the gifts — what the bunker brings
decisions.outcome: the_quartermaster proposed the gift list. (1) 2kg dried mushrooms (the bunker's trade surplus). (2) 1kg salt (the bunker has 260 days supply). (3) 5 doses of amoxicillin (the Cartographer said they do not have antibiotics — the_surgeon approved 5 doses from the reserve as a gift, not a trade, with the conservation protocol noted). (4) 1 grow light tube T5 (the bunker has 12; the Cartographer may have a use). (5) 1 hand-drawn map of the bunker's known zone (the Historian drew it — the bunker offers its knowledge in return for the Cartographer's). the_surgeon stated the 5 antibiotic doses are a gift that costs the bunker nothing it cannot spare and the Cartographer something it cannot make. the_council accepted the gifts.

decisions.item: the protocol — how the meeting is conducted
decisions.outcome: the_therapist proposed the meeting protocol. (1) the_courier arrives first, waits at the cache, does not approach. (2) the Cartographer arrives — the_courier does not stand, does not approach, remains seated. (3) the Cartographer sets the distance. (4) the_courier speaks first only if the Cartographer does not. (5) the_courier offers the gifts before asking the questions. (6) the meeting lasts as long as the Cartographer chooses. (7) the_courier does not invite the Cartographer to the bunker — the Cartographer offers or does not. the_therapist stated: the protocol is the thing that makes the meeting safe for both. The safety is the thing that makes the meeting possible. the_council accepted the protocol.

the_surgeon: select and package 5 amoxicillin doses with dosing instructions by Day 219

items.notes: The council meeting that was a preparation for a meeting. the_therapist said the protocol is the thing that makes the meeting safe. the_courier said the protocol is the thing that makes the meeting scary because the protocol means the meeting is real and the real is the thing you cannot rehearse. the_general said the real is the thing the bunker has been doing for 218 days. the_courier said the bunker is the thing he knows and the Cartographer is the thing he does not and the not-knowing is the scary part. the_therapist said the not-knowing is the part the Courier is best at — the Courier has walked to the unknown 4 times (Kilo, the warehouse, the agri depot, the municipal depot) and come back 4 times. the_courier said the coming back is the part he cannot promise. the_general said the coming back is the part the bunker cannot promise. the meeting ended with the understanding that the Day 220 meeting is the bunker's first diplomatic contact with a person who is not a trader, not a settler, and not a known quantity — the Cartographer is a walker, a mapper, a watcher, and the bunker's first neighbour who chose to come near.

agenda: the maps — what the Cartographer shared
the spring — the Cartographer's timeline confirmed

decisions.outcome: the_courier debriefed the council on the Day 220 meeting (diplomatic_contact_001). The meeting lasted 3 hours. The Cartographer is male, 50s, walks alone, maps the wasteland, maintains caches for other survivors, and studies the wolves as a ecological indicator. The Cartographer accepted the gifts, shared the maps, answered the questions, and asked for nothing except the bunker's continued willingness to leave notes at the cache. The Cartographer did not request entry to the bunker. The Cartographer offered to return to the cache on Day 250 with the spring planting maps. the_courier stated: the Cartographer is the most careful person I have met. He is careful the way the Hunter is careful. He watches before he moves. He does not move until he has watched. the_council accepted the debrief.

decisions.item: the maps — what the Cartographer shared
decisions.outcome: the_historian reported the maps the Cartographer shared (diplomatic_contact_001). The Cartographer gave the_courier 3 hand-drawn maps: (1) the fuel and water sources within 30km — the municipal depot (confirmed), 2 additional water sources, and 1 additional fuel source (a heating oil depot 22km north). (2) the low-dose zones — 4 zones within 20km where the surface dose is below 2 uSv/h, suitable for outdoor planting by Day 250-260. (3) the settlement map — 6 settlements within 50km, including the Verge (40 people, dark), Settlement 2 (the Freeholders, 60 people), the Shallows Market (3 merchants, transient), and 3 unknown settlements. the_historian stated: the maps are the most valuable intelligence the bunker has received. The Cartographer's maps are more detailed than the fire finder map (exp_report_fire_lookout_01) and cover the areas the bunker has not explored. the_council accepted the maps and authorised the_historian to cross-reference with the bunker's existing maps.

decisions.item: the spring — the Cartographer's timeline confirmed
decisions.outcome: the_meteorologist confirmed the Cartographer's spring timeline. The Cartographer estimates the surface will be plantable in the low-dose zones by Day 250-260. the_meteorologist's data (council_minutes_022 action item) confirms: particulate density down 30 percent, barometric pressure rising, wind southwest. the_meteorologist concurs with the Day 250-260 estimate. the_botanist stated: if the spring permits outdoor planting in the 4 low-dose zones, the bunker's food production moves from the greenhouse (15 percent of caloric need) to the surface (projected 40-60 percent within 90 days of planting). the_quartermaster stated: 40-60 percent is not survival. 40-60 percent is living. the_general stated: the spring is the thing the bunker has been waiting for without knowing it was waiting. The waiting is over. The spring is coming. The bunker must be ready to plant.

the_courier reported the Cartographer's knowledge of the Verge (rad_lineman_04). The Cartographer knows the Verge — 40 people, 6 shelters, micro-hydro on the river, the river froze, the battery is dead. The Cartographer has been to the Verge. The Verge is 30km east of the Cartographer's range. The Cartographer stated the Verge will not survive the winter without power. The Cartographer asked the bunker if the bunker can help. the_general stated: the Verge is the Kilo question again. 40 people, no power, winter. the_quartermaster stated: the bunker has fuel, antibiotics, and grow lights. The bunker can share. the_surgeon stated: the bunker has 5 doses to spare, not 40 people's worth. the_therapist stated: the Verge is not a medical question. The Verge is a fuel and light question. the_general stated: the council will decide on the Verge after the spring planting plan. The Verge is a question. The spring is the answer. The Verge waits for the spring with the bunker.

the_general proposed the relationship with the Cartographer. (1) The bunker leaves notes at the cache monthly. (2) The Cartographer returns to the cache on Day 250 with the spring planting maps. (3) The bunker offers the Cartographer standing access to the bunker's medical reserve (5 doses per visit, the_surgeon's conservation protocol) and the bunker's trade surplus (dried mushrooms, salt). (4) The Cartographer offers the bunker maps, intelligence, and the spring planting knowledge. (5) The relationship is a mutual aid agreement, not a trade agreement. The aid is given, not exchanged. the_council accepted the relationship framework. the_therapist stated: the relationship is the thing the bunker has been building since the Kilo mission. The Kilo mission was the bunker learning to give. The Cartographer is the bunker learning to receive. Both are the relationship. the_council concurred.

items.notes: The council meeting where the bunker's horizon expanded. The Cartographer gave the bunker maps of the world it has not seen. The spring is confirmed. The Verge is a question the bunker will answer. The relationship is a mutual aid agreement — the bunker gives medical and trade surplus, the Cartographer gives maps and knowledge. the_therapist said the Kilo mission was the bunker learning to give and the Cartographer is the bunker learning to receive. the_general said the bunker has been a closed door for 222 days. decisions.item: the second spring — zones 3 and 4 planting
decisions.outcome: the_botanist presented the second spring planting plan. Zone 3 (east ridge, surveyed patrol_debrief_035, 1.2 uSv/h, rocky soil) and zone 4 (north flat, surveyed patrol_debrief_035, 1.0 uSv/h, clay soil) are the second-year planting sites. Zone 3 will be planted with the clover (the Cartographer's gift, diplomatic_contact_005 — the clover feeds the bees) and the radish (the fastest crop, the first crop of the second spring). Zone 4 will be planted with the wheat (variety 2, the wetter-soil variety) and the oats. The winter rye in zone 1 will be the first harvest of the second spring (Day 370-380, the bridge). the_council approved the plan.

decisions.item: the bee colony expansion — the clover and the hollow oak
decisions.outcome: the_botanist presented the bee colony expansion plan. The bees are wintering in the hollow oak 3km southwest (diplomatic_contact_005). The bees will come out in the spring. The clover in zone 3 will feed the bees. The wildflowers in zone 1 will continue. The bees will expand — the_botanist estimates the colony will double in the second spring. The double is the thing the second spring does. The bees are the thing that doubles. the_council approved the plan.

decisions.item: the outdoor classroom — the second-year schedule
decisions.outcome: the_teacher presented the outdoor classroom schedule for the second year. The outdoor classroom will be daily, weather permitting, in zone 1 (the primary classroom) and zone 3 (the second classroom, for the clover and the bees). The outdoor classroom will teach: the water cycle (the first lesson, always), the soil (the ground), the bees (the pollination), the clover (the bee food), the winter rye (the bridge), and the word for year (the Child Soldier's first word of the second year, journal_raw_b3_80). The outdoor classroom is the thing that teaches the living. The living is the thing the second year is for. the_council approved the schedule.

decisions.item: the second-year ledger — the new words
decisions.outcome: the_quartermaster presented the second-year ledger. The first-year ledger had 12 words (source, reserve, shelf, growing, farm, herb, trade, community, bees, medicine, pollination, bridge). The second-year ledger adds 4 new words: clover (the bee food), hollow (the oak, the bees' winter home), snowflake (the second winter), and living (the thing the family does). The 16 words are the thing the family has. The 16 words are the thing the second year has. the_council accepted the ledger.
